messages:
Maya Chen: OK team — weird request: I'm rereading a pretty gnarly graphic novel and want a soundtrack for tonight. quick poll?
Riley: Yes please, love these pairing threads. what are the options?
Maya Chen: 1) late 70s jazz trio (smoky sax, low piano)
Maya Chen: 2) industrial / noise rock (harsh, abrasive)
Maya Chen: 3) slow synthwave (nostalgic, reverb-heavy)
Maya Chen: 4) field recordings / ambient (winds, distant hums)
Maya Chen: react with :one: :two: :three: or :four: — and drop quick recs if you have them
Sanjay Patel: :two: for me. Swans early stuff or some Mark Stewart vibes. gives the panels teeth.
Tess: If it's noir-leaning go :one:. Chet Baker at night, 10/10.
Devon: I like a 3->4 transition: start synthwave, then fade into field recordings for the epilogue. made a tiny playlist: https://open.spotify.com/playlist/fake-link-for-thread
Maya Chen: nice. starting to assemble. quick poll bot?
PollBot: Poll created by Maya Chen: "Graphic novel soundtrack" — 1️⃣ Jazz trio; 2️⃣ Industrial/noise; 3️⃣ Slow synthwave; 4️⃣ Field recordings/ambient. Ends in 2h.
Riley: voted :one: and :three:.
Sanjay Patel: voted :two:.
Tess: voted :one:.
Devon: voted :three:.
Maya Chen: voted :four: (for that fade into ambient idea). also any book recs that vibe with this pairing?
Riley: If you like gritty visuals, try 'Blacksad' or 'The Nikopol Trilogy' — both feel great with moody jazz.
Sanjay Patel: 'The Incal' for cosmic, try pairing with industrial synths.
Tess: for prose, 'Naked Lunch' reads weirdly nice with abrasive soundscapes.
Devon: Also 'The City & The City' for something eerie and understated — works with minimal synth.
Maya Chen: perfect recs. thanks all :heart: planning to do this tonight and report back with which combo actually made me finish the book.
